# Amendment history (generated by experiments/generate_amendment_history.py — do not edit by hand)

Generated by `experiments/generate_amendment_history.py` on 2026-10-17 at commit a24ee51-dirty from the git log, configs/registered_rules.json; do not edit by hand.

Every change to a registered rule since the baseline, taken from `Amends:` trailers in the git log. Edits to this file are overwritten by the next run; change a commit message, or add a trailer to a new commit, instead.

**Baseline.** `docs/preregistration_baseline_2026-10-15.md` is the registration exactly as it stood at the freeze of 15 October 2026, SHA-256 `08b02e8d303b61b4ebb4452266e54241c153b2600d58039bb5bb70dbb5e14104`, and is never edited. Amendments before that date are the in-document list inside the baseline itself; they were made before this mechanism existed and are not reconstructed here, because the commits of that period carry no trailers and a reconstruction would assert dates the log cannot support.

**Current values** live in `configs/registered_rules.json` (9 rules) and are asserted against the implementation by `tests/test_registration_matches_the_code.py`. This file says how they got there; that file says they are still true.

## Amendments

None since the baseline. An empty list here means no commit has carried an `Amends:` trailer, which is not the same as no rule having changed — a change made without a trailer leaves no entry, and `tests/test_registration_matches_the_code.py` is what catches that.
